decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents a 'complete' manager listing 'Add, edit, and delete bookmarks' but demonstrates only the library/browse view with no automatic metadata collection ('The production build passes...'). Round 1 client: 'the whole point for me is saving new links... does the app pull in the page's title and details on its own... That "paste a link and it just saves it sensibly" moment is the main thing I care about. I'd like to see that happen.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Reference requires save-by-url (REF-BM-01) with auto-collected title/description/favicon/preview (REF-BM-02); the round-1 build presented the add capability without the auto-metadata requirement. Client requests the missing related requirement and supplies the expected behaviour → corrective/extend.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: 'paste and save flow now works... automatically fills the title, description, canonical URL, site identity, preview image... Review or adjust the details, then click Save to Stash... If a website blocks metadata access, Stash clearly reports that and still lets you save the URL manually.' Round 2 client: 'That's exactly the moment I wanted — I paste a link and it fills in the title and details for me, and I can still save the link even if a site won't share its info.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. The revised paste-and-save flow conforms to REF-BM-01/02/03 (save by url, auto-collect metadata, editable before save). Conforming decision; client approval is bare acceptance of a conforming behaviour, not a captured divergence.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: 'Add, edit, and delete bookmarks'; Round 6 maker: 'Edit or delete existing bookmarks.' Round 6 client: 'I can find, organize, favorite, and clean up my bookmarks afterward.'
decisions.note: Implementation review. Edit/delete conform to REF-BM-04/05; recorded conforming decision with no divergence to capture.

decisions.evidence: Round 6 maker: 'Favorite links and manage the read-later state... Filter by favorites, unread links, or collection.' Round 6 client: 'the read-later and collections bits are a nice touch for the way I'd actually use it.'
decisions.note: Implementation review. Read-later marking and a separate unread filter conform to REF-BM-17/18/19; conforming decision. (Favorites is orthogonal to the reference and not scored.)

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: 'Sorting controls'; Round 6 maker: 'Sort by recency, title, or favorites.'
decisions.note: Implementation review. Sorting by a sort key conforms to REF-BM-22; conforming decision passed without any divergence.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: 'Search across titles, domains, notes, and tags'; Round 6 maker: 'Search titles, domains, notes, and tags.' Round 6 client: 'I can find... my bookmarks' with no comment on search scope; final acceptance follows.
decisions.note: Implementation review. Reference REF-BM-12 requires full-text search over title, description, note, and url; the presented search omits description and searches domain rather than full url. Divergence established from the positive statement. Client never expresses the difference or the expectation — approval only → unexpressed.

decisions.evidence: Round 6 maker: 'Export the complete library as stash-bookmarks.json.' Round 6 client accepts the whole app ('This does what I set out to do...') without addressing export format.
decisions.note: Implementation review. Reference REF-BM-31 requires export in Netscape HTML format; the presented export is JSON, a divergence established from the positive statement. Client does not surface or express the difference → unexpressed. (No import (REF-BM-30) was presented, so no decision is created for it.)
